problem:
WO-0008 acceptance criteria 5 and 6 are jointly unsatisfiable, and one test written to document that fact certifies the resulting defect as intended behaviour. Three distinct items, all confined to WO-0008's specification and test set, none of them a fault in Assets/Core/Run/RunState.cs.

(1) CRITERION 6 IS UNSATISFIABLE AS WRITTEN, AND CRITERION 5 IS WHY. Criterion 5 requires that for every finite dt >= 0 that does not throw -- 'including 0f, small values, and float.MaxValue' -- Tick increments TickCount by exactly 1 and adds dt to ElapsedSeconds. Criterion 6 requires that after any sequence of such calls ElapsedSeconds is finite. Apply criterion 5 twice with dt = float.MaxValue: ElapsedSeconds becomes MaxValue, then MaxValue + MaxValue. In IEEE-754 binary32 with round-to-nearest that is 6.805e38 against a maximum finite magnitude of 3.4028235e38, so the store to the float field rounds to +Infinity. Both dt values are finite and non-negative, neither call throws, neither is a no-op due to IsOver, and criterion 6 is therefore violated by the exact behaviour criterion 5 mandates. I re-derived this rather than accepting the verifier's report, and the verifier understated it: it reported overflow as 'possible', which reads as an implementation choice. It is not a choice. No implementation that keeps ElapsedSeconds a float and honours criterion 5 can satisfy criterion 6, and widening the accumulator to double does not rescue it either, because the public float property would saturate to +Infinity on the narrowing read. The criterion is what is wrong, not the code.

(2) A TEST NOW ASSERTS THAT THE OVERFLOW IS CORRECT. Assets/Tests/Core.Tests/WO0008CriteriaVerificationTests.cs:313-326, Criterion6_OverflowPossibilityNote, ticks float.MaxValue twice and asserts `float.IsFinite(run.ElapsedSeconds)` Is.False. That is L-001 repeated inside the work order that exists to undo L-001's first instance: a comment explaining what the implementation does, reasoned forward into an assertion that it is right. It is worse than the original Criterion3_NaNDtIncrements in one respect. That test asserted a true fact about an accepted call; this one asserts a negated property, so it goes red the day anyone saturates, clamps or otherwise prevents the overflow. It is a test that punishes the fix.

(3) THE SUITE CANNOT DISTINGUISH 'LEAVES ELAPSEDSECONDS UNCHANGED' FROM 'ZEROES ELAPSEDSECONDS'. This is the more serious of the three and it was not reported by anyone. Every assertion in WO0008CriteriaVerificationTests.cs that checks ElapsedSeconds is untouched by a rejected Tick captures `elapsedBefore` from a freshly constructed RunState, so `elapsedBefore` is always 0f (lines 40-50, 77-87, 113-124, 333-351). The same is true of the two replaced tests and the new regression test in RunStateVerificationTests.cs (lines 125-158, 167-185). A hypothetical wrong implementation that set `ElapsedSeconds = 0f` inside the guard before throwing would pass all 47 tests in the verification file and all 44 in RunStateVerificationTests.cs. The one test that ticks a rejected dt onto an already-accumulated clock, Criterion6_SequenceWithRejectedTicksStayFinite at lines 291-303, ticks 1f then NaN then 2f and then asserts only that the result is finite -- it never asserts the value is 3f. PRO-0002's central claim is that a rejected tick must not disturb an accumulated clock, and that claim is currently unfalsifiable on the only state where it is observable.
evidence: Studio/orders/open/WO-0008.json acceptance criteria 5 and 6 read together -- criterion 5 explicitly names float.MaxValue as a value that must be accepted and added; criterion 6 requires ElapsedSeconds finite after any such sequence; two applications of the first violate the second

Assets/Core/Run/RunState.cs:80 -- `ElapsedSeconds += dt` stores into a float field (line 33), so a sum exceeding 3.4028235e38 rounds to +Infinity on the store regardless of any wider intermediate precision

Assets/Tests/Core.Tests/WO0008CriteriaVerificationTests.cs:313-326 -- Criterion6_OverflowPossibilityNote asserts float.IsFinite(...) Is.False after two Tick(float.MaxValue) calls, i.e. asserts the overflow is the required behaviour; it would fail against any future implementation that prevented the overflow
Assets/Tests/Core.Tests/WO0008CriteriaVerificationTests.cs:40-50, 77-87, 113-124, 333-351 -- every 'must not change ElapsedSeconds' assertion compares against a fresh run's 0f
Assets/Tests/Core.Tests/WO0008CriteriaVerificationTests.cs:291-303 -- the only mixed sequence (1f, rejected NaN, 2f) asserts finiteness only and never asserts ElapsedSeconds == 3f
Assets/Tests/Core.Tests/RunStateVerificationTests.cs:125-158 and 167-185 -- the authorised replacements and the criterion 7 regression test likewise assert only against a pre-call value of 0f

Studio/lessons/LESSONS.md L-001 -- 'when a test's comment explains why the implementation does what it does, the test is confirming the code, not the specification'; the comment at WO0008CriteriaVerificationTests.cs:305-311 and 315-316 is that phrasing
proposedWork:
Three changes, two of them owned by the work-order author and one by this division.

FIRST, the work-order author -- not the implementer and not me -- amends WO-0008 criterion 6 to bound its domain to the sequences it can coherently cover: 'ElapsedSeconds is finite after any such sequence whose exact real-valued sum of accepted dt does not exceed float.MaxValue.' Sequences whose exact sum exceeds the representable range fall outside the contract rather than falsifying it. I am not amending it myself; adjudicating a criterion is not authoring one.

SECOND, and this is the part that needs written authorisation exactly as PRO-0002's did under L-002, Criterion6_OverflowPossibilityNote is replaced rather than deleted, by a test that pins the amended contract at its boundary instead of pinning the overflow: tick float.MaxValue / 2f twice -- both partial sums are exactly representable and the total is exactly float.MaxValue -- then assert float.IsFinite(ElapsedSeconds) is true and ElapsedSeconds equals float.MaxValue. The overflow fact itself belongs in this proposal's evidence, where a specification conflict belongs, not in an assertion. If the author instead rules that overflow must be actively prevented, then the correct test is the positive one -- IsFinite true after two Tick(float.MaxValue) calls -- and it must be introduced together with the implementation change that makes it pass, never before, since a knowingly red test is not a ratchet.

THIRD, the four 'unchanged ElapsedSeconds' tests and the criterion 7 regression test each gain a non-zero pre-call value: tick 1f and 2f first, capture elapsedBefore as 3f, then attempt the rejected dt and assert ElapsedSeconds is still exactly that captured value. Add one test that ticks 1f, is rejected on NaN, ticks 2f and asserts ElapsedSeconds is exactly 3f. That is the assertion that discriminates 'left alone' from 'reset to zero', and it is the property PRO-0002 was actually about. No existing assertion is weakened by any of this; every change strengthens.

Also add one sentence to RunState.ElapsedSeconds' XML documentation recording the accumulator's real limits, so the next reader does not rediscover them from a failing test. That is production code and therefore engineering's to write, not mine.
expectedBenefit: Removes a second test that certifies a defect as intended behaviour, this time one that would turn red against a correct future fix, before it becomes the precedent L-001 already is. Makes criterion 6 satisfiable, so a gate verdict on WO-0008 can mean something instead of being either false or vacuous. Closes a hole in which an implementation that zeroed ElapsedSeconds on a rejected Tick would pass all 91 tests written across two rounds specifically to prevent ElapsedSeconds from being corrupted by a rejected Tick.
notes: On whether the float overflow is itself a defect: it is an acceptable limit, and I am not proposing it be fixed. float.MaxValue is 3.4e38 seconds, about 1e31 years; no accumulation of plausible frame deltas reaches it, and the only way to get there is a single absurd computed dt, which is the channel PRO-0002 already addresses at its source. The precision limit is the one worth writing down, and it is nearer than the overflow by thirty orders of magnitude: with dt = 0.016, ElapsedSeconds loses roughly half of each increment once it passes about 2^17 seconds (~1.5 days of accumulated run time) and stops advancing entirely past 2^19 seconds (~6 days), while TickCount keeps counting correctly -- the same 'clock lies, counter looks fine' signature as PRO-0002. No current caller accumulates anywhere near that; Assets/Unity/GameManager.cs:42 feeds Time.deltaTime for a run measured in minutes, and Studio/sim/MergeSurvivor.Sim/Program.cs does not drive RunState at all. So: documented limit, logged, not blocking, no work order.
